business_scope.primary_industry_name: Industrial Quick-Freezing of Steamed Dim Sum and Dumplings

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners, as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; CSSF AML/CFT circulars and Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) guidelines.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Passport/ID Authority, Bank or Notary in Country of Origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/CFT Source of Funds and Source of Wealth Declaration for Each UBO
Standard Beneficial Owner Declaration for the Luxembourg UBO Register (RBE)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Business Registers / UBO Register Filing Portal

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, limited partners and authorized signatories against the United Nations, EU, OFAC, and Luxembourg national consolidated sanctions lists; mandatory Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) screening at onboarding and on an ongoing basis; enhanced due diligence where a PEP, higher-risk jurisdiction or unusual ownership structure is identified; compliance with the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF AML/CFT circulars; documentary verification of identity, source of funds and source of wealth for all UBOs.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), available at https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be submitted in French, German or Luxembourgish, but Latin-script transliteration is accepted for use before the RCS; if the intended name is in non-Latin script, a faithful Latin-alphabet phonetic or equivalent transliteration must be provided and must not create confusion with existing registered names. The legal suffix 'SCSp' or 'S.C.Sp.' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' is required to indicate the corporate form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of a name rejection, the applicant or the Luxembourg-licensed professional filing the request may file a written administrative appeal with the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) requesting reconsideration, attaching a fresh RCS negative certificate and a legal supporting opinion; if the administrative appeal fails, judicial review may be sought before the Luxembourg administrative tribunal within three months of the administrative refusal decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office alone is generally not acceptable for RCS registration of an SCSp; the partnership must maintain a registered office physically located in Luxembourg and a genuine administrative seat; for a frozen food manufacturing operation, physical production and warehousing premises will be required for the underlying operating subsidiary, while the SCSp itself may rely on a professional registered-office provider only if the provider offers genuine substance administration and the RCS filing shows a real Luxembourg address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk for an active industrial registration is estimated at 35% per year; unannounced physical on-site inspections are reasonably likely where tax, customs, food-safety and LBR authorities cross-check registered office, production premises, stock and staffing.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (LCS), Part on the Special Limited Partnership (SCSp) introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013, Articles 101-1 to 101-15 LCS; Law of 19 December 2008 on the Luxembourg Business Registers; Law of 15 May 2018 on Environmental Impact Assessment for associated operational permitting.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 3-5 Place du Saint-Esprit, L-1478 Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Constitutive Deed / Deed of Partnership (Acte constitutif) executed before a Luxembourg notary or by private writing registered with the Administration de l'Enregistrement; filed with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SCSp has no statutory minimum capital. It must comprise at least one general partner (commandité) with unlimited liability and at least one limited partner (commanditaire). Contributions may be in cash or in kind and are freely determined by the partners; Luxembourg law imposes neither full pre-payment nor a deposit into a blocked escrow account for SCSp registration. The constitutive deed must record the value and payment terms of each subscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a founding general assembly of the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) held at its registered office, the following resolutions were unanimously adopted. FIRST: the Deed of Constitution and Partnership Agreement are approved and adopted; the partners' subscriptions to the partnership interests are accepted according to the contribution schedule. SECOND: the registered office of the Partnership is established at [address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. THIRD: [Name] is appointed Manager (Gérant/General Partner), with full power to bind the Partnership, open bank accounts, and sign all agreements. FOURTH: the Manager is authorized to complete Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) registration, secure business establishment and food-safety permits, and file all tax and social security registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Registration of the Constitutive Deed (Acte Constitutif)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public; Administration de l'Enregistrement et des Domaines (AED)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Luxembourg notary to draft and execute the SCSp constitutive deed and partnership agreement. Verify the identity and capacity of the general partner and each limited partner, define the contribution schedule (cash and/or in-kind), the profit-share ratios, the duration, and the registered office. Obtain the landlord's acceptance of the registered office. If a private-writing deed is chosen, register it at the AED for stamping and legal filing.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement / Deed of Constitution
Passport copies and residence proofs of all founding partners
Certificate of good standing and LEI for corporate partners
Registered office acceptance letter signed by the building owner
Evidence of valuation for in-kind contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or AED raises a query, execute a supplemental rectificative deed (acte rectificatif) and re-register the corrected document; missing partner signatures are cured by filing a notarized power of attorney retroactively.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of signature, file the constitutive deed with the RCS through the LBR electronic filing portal, together with the completed application form, the registered office acceptance, and the manager's consent. Pay the LBR fee online; the RCS issues the registration number (matricule) and publishes the entry free of charge in RESA. The extract is used as proof of legal existence for all subsequent administrative procedures.
required_dossiers: Constitutive deed (authentic or private-writing)
RCS registration application form
Registered office acceptance letter
Consent of the appointed manager to act
Proof of payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS serves a rectification notice, cure the identified deficiencies within the indicated deadline by uploading certified documents or translations; a refusal may be challenged before the Luxembourg District Court (civil chamber) within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for SMEs and Entrepreneurship (Guichet.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the establishment authorization application with the Ministry of the Economy through the Guichet.lu e-portal. Evidence of the manager's professional qualifications in food manufacturing, a clean criminal record, and proof of financial capacity must accompany the application. The authorization is a precondition for commencing industrial operations and for the subsequent social security registration of employees.
required_dossiers: Duly filed Guichet.lu application form
Extract from the criminal records of the manager (Luxembourg and previous countries of residence)
Professional qualification diplomas or experience certificates
RCS registration extract
Bank reference or proof of financial capacity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The applicant may be granted a grace period to supplement the file; if the application is refused, the applicant may re-apply with an amended professional qualification file or bring an administrative appeal before the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within three months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial Environmental Permit and EIA Determination
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'environnement – Ministry of Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the environmental permit application, including the EIA screening determination, in accordance with the Law of 15 May 2018. Describe the blast-freezing and cooking processes, capacity, refrigeration gases, wastewater, VOC and odor emission points, noise levels, and waste streams. The environmental permit fixes emission limit values, self-monitoring, and reporting obligations before production start-up.
required_dossiers: Environmental permit application form
EIA screening report or, if required, full EIA report
Process flow diagrams and facility layout
Wastewater discharge plan and pre-treatment design
Noise, odor, and air-emission assessment
Waste classification and disposal plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Administration de l'environnement will formally request missing information; failure to respond leads to rejection. The applicant may lodge an administrative appeal or resubmit a perfected application after carrying out the corrective studies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Safety Approval and Occupational Health & Fire Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Veterinary and Food Administration (ALVA); Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); communal fire inspection service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the factory as a food business operator under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and, insofar as dim sum fillings contain meat or seafood, obtain approval of the establishment under Regulation (EC) No 853/2004. Implement HACCP, allergen control, cold chain, and traceability systems. Simultaneously obtain the fire safety certificate, structural load clearance for freezers and production lines, and the ITM workplace safety and occupational health approval.
required_dossiers: ALVA food business notification or registration form
HACCP plan and prerequisite-program documentation
Approval dossier under Regulation (EC) No 853/2004 (if animal-derived ingredients are used)
Fire safety certificate issued by the commune
Structural load inspection report by a licensed engineer
ITM occupational risk assessment and staff training register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ALVA or ITM identifies non-conformities, a corrective action plan must be filed within the set deadline and a re-inspection scheduled; repeated failure may suspend start-up, but the operator may request an administrative review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, Social Security, and EORI Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); Administration de l'Enregistrement et des Domaines (AED); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, obtain the Luxembourg national identification number (NIF) for the SCSp from the ACD and register the employer account with the CCSS. Submit VAT registration to the AED (food supplies may qualify for reduced rates; registration is mandatory above the VAT threshold). The partnership, although fiscally transparent for income tax purposes, remains a taxable person for VAT and must file periodic returns. Apply for an EORI number if the factory will export frozen dim sum outside the European Union.
required_dossiers: RCS extract with matricule
Constitutive deed and managerial authorizations
Proof of registered office and bank account
Turnover forecast for VAT scheme election
EORI registration application (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fiscal or social administrations flag incorrect data, file a corrective declaration using the RCS extract; voluntary late registration generally mitigates penalties; appeals lie with the Director of ACD/AED or the Social Security Arbitration Board.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (General Directorate for SMEs and Entrepreneurship) for the Autorisation d'établissement; Luxembourg Veterinary and Food Administration (ALVA) for food business licensing; Administration de l'environnement for environmental permitting; Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) for occupational clearance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Establishment Authorization (Autorisation d'établissement), Food Business Operator Approval (agrément) under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and No 853/2004, and Environmental Operating Permit (Autorisation environnementale).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Agency), Ministry of Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Mandatory EIA screening under the Law of 15 May 2018 (Annex IV – installations for the manufacture of food products); a full EIA report is triggered if the finished-product capacity exceeds 75 tonnes per day or if the site lies in or near a protected zone such as Natura 2000. The final tier is confirmed by the formal screening determination.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Grand-Ducal wastewater discharge regulations and municipal sewer pre-treatment bylaws; VOC and odor emissions limited per the European Industrial Emissions Directive framework; process refrigerants per EU F-gas Regulation No 517/2014; food waste separation and disposal under the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste management; noise levels restricted to applicable industrial-zone limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) issued by the communal fire inspection service; structural load verification for blast freezers, steam lines, and production machinery signed by an accredited structural engineer; workplace clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), including occupational risk assessment, electrical safety inspection, and an employee health surveillance program approved by the occupational physician.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for income/corporate taxation; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT registration, returns, and indirect tax compliance. Official portals: Guichet.lu / MyGuichet.lu (electronic filings), Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) for the RCS matricule, and the AED eTVA electronic declaration system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Establish the SCSp by notarized limited partnership agreement and publish the constitutive act with the RCS via the Luxembourg Business Registers platform to obtain the 14-digit national business registration number (matricule). Step 2: Submit the AED VAT identification declaration (form 44) electronically through MyGuichet.lu, accompanied by the RCS extract, partnership agreement, and identity documentation of the general partner and limited partners. Step 3: AED issues the Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits) normally within 2–4 weeks; a non-EU-established partner or foreign taxable person carrying out taxable supplies in Luxembourg must simultaneously appoint a Luxembourg fiscal representative under Article 61 of the Luxembourg VAT Law (Statute of 12 February 1979) unless covered by the non-established Union OSS / Import OSS schemes. Step 4: The SCSp must also register as an intra-Community operator (DEB identification) for goods movements and file recapitulative statements. ACD and AED compliance is coordinated through the single RCS matricule for all domestic filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the SCSp is fiscally transparent (look-through) by default; profits, deductions, and VAT-relevant activities are attributed directly to general and limited partners, whether resident, EU, or non-resident. Territorial scope: Luxembourg taxation arises only at the partner level on the SCSp net income allocable to each partner; non-resident partners are taxable in Luxembourg only on Luxembourg-source partnership income and are generally protected by the applicable double tax treaty. The entity itself is not subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax; no minimum statutory capital is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Statutory check-the-box election: the SCSp may elect, under Luxembourg income tax law (LIR Article 182bis), to be taxed as a capital company (opaque regime) where at least one partner is subject to corporate income tax or where all partners hold their interests as business assets; the election binds the partnership for at least five years and must be submitted with the ACD before the end of the first taxable year. US-style check-the-box classifications are respected for federal tax characterization but remain subject to Luxembourg hybrid-mismatch rules transposing ATAD (LIR Articles 168quinquies and 168sexies), which may recharacterize the SCSp or deny deductions where the partner jurisdiction treats it as opaque; single-entity tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) is not available to transparent SCSp vehicles, but Luxembourg VAT grouping under Article 62 of the VAT Law remains available where joint VAT liability and financial, economic, and organizational links are satisfied.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée) governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, as amended, and EU VAT Directives. Headline standard rate 17%; intermediate rate 14%; reduced rate 8%; super-reduced rate 3% for basic foodstuffs (pre-cooked frozen dim sum qualifies domestically at 3% where not exported); zero rating applies to qualifying exports and certain intra-Community and international transport supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (VAT small undertaking exemption under the Luxembourg VAT Law), exclusive of VAT; the exemption is not available to non-resident taxable persons, taxable persons making exempt financial/real-estate supplies with input VAT recovery, or supplies of goods destined for importation; intra-EU distance-selling registration threshold for foreign established suppliers is EUR 10,000 (no threshold for imports or for services subject to the reverse charge); the Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) relief applies to low-value consignments of goods up to EUR 150 imported into Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national real-time fiscal-clearance server exists in Luxembourg (contrast with Italy's SDI), but electronic invoicing is mandatory for B2G transactions since 1 November 2021 using the PEPPOL network and the European standard EN 16931 (LuxML format). A nationwide mandatory B2B e-invoicing regime was announced by the Luxembourg Government and is expected to be phased in by 2026, requiring structured electronic invoices via PEPPOL-compliant service providers. VAT returns and recapitulative statements (EC Sales Lists) must be filed electronically through the AED eTVA/MyGuichet.lu portal; the DEB (Intrastat) declarations apply to goods movements where applicable; digital stamping or pre-clearance of invoices is currently not imposed on food-exporting factories.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of frozen dim sum and dumplings physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union qualify for the 0% VAT rate under Article 43 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, provided the factory holds conclusive proof of removal from the EU territory within the statutory time frame (generally evidenced by a customs export declaration and transport documents). Sales to VAT-identified EU business customers qualify as zero-rated intra-Community supplies under Article 46 LTV with EC Sales List reporting and validation of the customer's valid LU/other EU VAT number; services directly connected with the exported goods (e.g., freezing, packaging, and processing work performed on movable goods destined for non-EU customers) may also qualify for zero rating where the related goods are dispatched outside the EU. Proof of export must be retained and available at the time the VAT return is filed; the AED may request further evidence, and the zero rate is denied where the goods are released for free circulation within the EU or consumed domestically.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document released via Luxembourg Customs / the EU Ex-Dat electronic export system evidencing exit from the EU)
Transport evidence: Bill of Lading (maritime), CMR International Consignment Note (road), or Air Waybill (air) confirming physical dispatch from Luxembourg territory
Commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, and warehouse dispatch records demonstrating consignment identity and revenue traceability
Inward Remittance Certificate: bank SWIFT MT103 / Letter of Credit settlement documentation evidencing repatriation of export value (benchmark evidence used by the AED in substantiation audits)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AED applies risk-based audit algorithms to export zero-rating claims and is empowered to demand the full documentation bundle within a specified response period; failure to substantiate the EU exit leads to retrospective re-invoicing of VAT at the domestic food rate (3%) or the standard rate (17%), together with recovery of input VAT disallowed, late-payment interest of 0.8% per month (or part thereof), and administrative fines. Fraudulent zero-rating or document falsification constitutes VAT fraud under Articles 59 and 62 of the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 and may be prosecuted criminally with fines, imprisonment, and publication or disqualification measures; the law prescribes an extended 10-year limitation period for fraudulent tax evasion and joint and several liability may be asserted against the SCSp's general partner and any tax representative. In serious cases, the judicial authorities may also trigger EU follow-up via the Eurofisc network and OLAF cross-border cooperation, exposing the exporter to parallel administrative and criminal clawback actions in multiple member states.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); monetary policy competence is vested in the European Central Bank (ECB); prudential banking supervision is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); there is no separate foreign exchange administration because Luxembourg is a Eurozone member and applies the EU free-movement-of-capital regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union; no exchange-control authorisation is required for cross-border payments, trade settlements, or profit remittances. The SCSp is fiscally transparent, so profit distributions to partners are generally not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax, provided the partnership does not carry on a Luxembourg commercial activity that triggers entity-level taxation; residual Luxembourg-source income benefits from treaty-based reductions where the partner is resident in a treaty jurisdiction. Capital outflows are unrestricted, and repatriation hurdles are limited to standard anti-money-laundering (AML) due diligence and statistical balance-of-payments reporting obligations to the BCL.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement exists in Luxembourg or the Eurozone; export receipts may be held freely in any currency, and no mandatory conversion ratio applies. EU law prohibits exchange controls, so the SCSp is not required to convert, repatriate, or deposit export receipts within any prescribed timeline; only bank-level AML screening and the BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting thresholds apply, and the tax authorities require standard commercial documentation for the underlying frozen-food export transactions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility for routine operational collections and supplier payments through CSSF-authorised Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) passporting under EU PSD2/EMD2; however, EMIs cannot issue documentary letters of credit (MT700), cannot hold funds as deposits protected by the Luxembourg deposit guarantee scheme (FGDL), are ineligible for credit intermediation, and operate under e-money issuance caps imposed by their CSSF licence; therefore, Low viability for capital escrow and trade-finance treasury functions. Legal constraint: safeguarding rules require e-money funds to be held in segregated pooled accounts, so the SCSp should confine EMI usage to sub-threshold operational flows and maintain its primary treasury and escrow accounts at a tier-1 credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the authorised manager (Gérant) of the SCSp, or of a duly mandated officer holding a valid power of attorney, is the de facto industry standard for first-time onboarding of non-resident partnerships; remote video onboarding is generally limited to entities already owning a relationship within the same banking group or through a Luxembourg branch of the client's home bank. For a newly formed SCSp, at least one in-person compliance interview in Luxembourg is effectively mandatory, accompanied by notarised, apostilled constitutional documents and verified identity documentation of all authorised signatories and ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-tier ownership and non-resident limited partners (commanditaires) creating beneficial-ownership opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated extract from the Luxembourg Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), full organisational chart, certified passports and proof of residential address for all UBOs, partnership agreement (Pacte Social), capital contribution ledgers, and sworn source-of-wealth statements supported by bank reference letters from the originating institutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-transparent SCSp classification raising doubts as to the source of funds and economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg tax residency certificate or attestation from the Administration des contributions directes confirming fiscal transparency, audited capital accounts, and a substance file demonstrating the Gérant's Luxembourg residence, local decision-making authority, premises lease, and payroll records for Luxembourg-based personnel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border food-trade counterparties located in high-risk or partially sanctioned jurisdictions affecting payment routing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Positive sanctions-screening certificates, targeted OFAC/EU/UN sanctions-list checks, commercial contracts, proforma invoices, bills of lading, customs declarations, and third-party enhanced due diligence reports evidencing genuine trade underlying every routed payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid aggregation of export proceeds or irregular cash-flow volatility inconsistent with the declared frozen-food production model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Annual audited financial statements, production-capacity certificates, purchase orders from major distributors, warehouse inventory reports, and executed bank comfort letters from both originating and receiving financial institutions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from each partner's own bank account to the SCSp operational account, using a purpose code designating direct investment / capital contribution (Luxembourg balance-of-payments statistical code for equity injections) and a reference narrative citing the capital contribution agreement. The receiving bank may request a BCL balance-of-payments declaration for cross-border financial transactions above applicable statistical thresholds. No BCL approval is required; however, the transfer file must include the RBE extract, partner resolutions, the notarised contribution deed, a verification letter confirming the partner's ownership of the remitting account, and source-of-wealth documentation to satisfy CSSF AML directives.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Two primary clearing rails are deployed for the industrial quick-freezing operation: (1) SWIFT MT103/MT202 wire transfers for direct TT settlement with raw-material suppliers of frozen seafood, flour, seasonings, and packaging materials in Asia and the Americas; and (2) Commercial Letters of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700 and amended via MT707 for documentary trade settlement of high-value commodity purchase contracts. For eurozone suppliers, ordinary SEPA Credit Transfers or instant SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT Inst) provide the most cost-effective rail. All payment instructions must be matched against underlying purchase orders, import customs declarations, shipping documents, and quality-inspection certificates to satisfy Luxembourg AML law and the CSSF's KYC obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX outright forwards (deliverable EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, and other liquid currency pairs) executed with a licensed Luxembourg bank or EU credit institution

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) for counterpart currencies with restricted deliverability, entered only where the underlying exposure is a genuine commercial obligation of the frozen-food import/export trade flows
Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) aligned with long-term capital injections, partner loans, or supplier-financing cash-flow profiles

FX swaps (spot-forward rollovers) for working-capital liquidity management, subject to EMIR margin, reporting, and risk-mitigation obligations applicable to non-financial counterparties below the clearing threshold

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of registration details filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following approval of annual accounts by the general partner; for pass-through SCSp entities without accounting publication duty, confirmation due by registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines up to EUR 5,000; persistent default may trigger court-ordered compulsory liquidation and administrative strike-off from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and partnership information return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May following the tax year; extension to 31 December available where a tax advisor is retained
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; late-filing penalties up to EUR 5,000; potential director liability for non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return where the SCSp is registered for VAT due to business activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly returns due by the 15th day of the month following the reporting period; annual return due by 1 May for taxpayers under the annual scheme
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EUR 750 per return; default interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid VAT; additional penalties up to EUR 5,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax return for taxable assets attributed to Luxembourg-resident general partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Wealth Tax Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May following the tax year; extension to 31 December available where a tax advisor is retained
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 0.6% per month; late-filing penalties up to EUR 5,000; enforced collection through distraint

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership filed with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of any change; annual confirmation required at least once per calendar year by the registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines from EUR 500 to EUR 12,500 per violation; publication of penalties; restriction on distributions and dismissal of claims in court proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit not required for the SCSp as a pass-through vehicle; audit obligation may arise where a general partner is itself an audited entity, where creditors holding at least half of the capital request an audit, or where the partnership exceeds two of three thresholds: balance sheet total > EUR 4.4 million, net turnover > EUR 8.8 million, and average headcount > 50; consolidated group rules may also trigger audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 as amended, implementing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as adopted by the EU permitted for certain undertakings

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must confirm its beneficial ownership data with the RBE annually, irrespective of shareholding transfers; any transfer must be reported within one month; the confirmation re-validates the identity, nationality, and nature of control of each beneficial owner; failure to maintain accurate RBE data exposes the partnership to criminal fines and procedural sanctions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 3,000 per annum for registered office, local corporate agent, and domiciliation services in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 15,000 per annum for voluntary or mandatory statutory audit, depending on the partnership's asset and transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at SCSp entity level due to fiscal transparency; for Luxembourg-resident corporate partners, combined CIT + solidarity surcharge + municipal business tax = 24.94% in Luxembourg City (range approx. 20.99%-24.94% depending on commune)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box exemption of 80% on qualifying IP income; participation exemption on dividends and capital gains (95% or 100% based on participation); tax credits for investments and digitalization; no sector-specific tax holiday for frozen-dumpling production, but available accelerated depreciation for clean-tech and food-processing equipment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1001 (Annual Tax Return for Corporate/Commercial Entities) filed via MyLuxTax / e-CDF portal of the Luxembourg tax authority (Administration des contributions directes); may be complemented by Form 1002 (Municipal Business Tax) for corporate partners carrying on business through a permanent establishment; SCSp itself files an informational annex.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 30 June of the calendar year following the close of the fiscal year (for 31 December year-end); administrative extension to 31 December generally granted on application; extension not automatic for SCSp if no taxable basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal and administrative identification of the SCSp: name, CNI/LCAP number, registered office address, list of gérants (managers) and commercial registry number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident managers or partners must provide their foreign tax identification numbers and residence addresses; individuals additionally provide nationality and birth details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of worldwide accounting profit/loss under Luxembourg GAAP (IFRS optional), including turnover from frozen dim-sum/dumpling production, cost of sales, operating expenses, depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the taxable income attributable to the Luxembourg commercial activity; foreign partners are not required to disclose unrelated offshore income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determination of the taxable basis before allocation: adjustments for non-deductible expenses, transfer pricing adjustments, and any participation exemption or IP box deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should ensure that any income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment is clearly separated from passive profit shares.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of the taxable basis (profit/loss) among partners: for each partner, their share percentage, profit allocation, and tax classification status (resident/non-resident, corporate/individual).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, provide treaty residence and confirm entitlement to benefits; attach Form No. 1 for treaty relief if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of tax credits and withholding taxes: advance corporate tax payments, foreign tax credits, 80% IP regime credits, and other deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should not claim Luxembourg personal credits; these are generally limited to residents unless provided in the DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronic signature and authorization: signature by the gérant or statutory representative and reference to the accountant/authorised tax agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A proxy (power of attorney) must be submitted for non-resident representatives; online authentication via LuxTrust token is mandatory.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: interest of 0.6% per month or part of a month on unpaid taxes; late-filing fine up to EUR 7,500 and 10% penalty on assessed tax. Non-filing after notice may trigger tax assessment ex officio plus 20% increase; criminal fraud penalty for deliberate omissions (see red flags below).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions made by an SCSp to its partners because the SCSp is tax transparent and distributions are not classified as dividends. Dividends paid by a Luxembourg capital company to individuals (if applicable) are subject to 15% withholding tax, but the SCSp structure avoids this layer.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Where a partner is a resident of a tax treaty jurisdiction, treaty relief is invoked by filing an application for a tax clearance/withholding tax abatement with the Luxembourg direct tax administration using Form 1 (or Form 1-A). The partner must provide: (i) a valid Tax Residence Certificate issued by the treaty state for the relevant calendar year, (ii) an entity-specific beneficial ownership declaration, and (iii) confirmation of no abuse/hybrid mismatch. The administration issues an abatement certificate within 3-6 months; refund route available if withholding applied at source.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law applies 0% withholding tax on cross-border interest and royalties paid by a Luxembourg payer, with limited exceptions under the dated EU Savings Directive. Treaty rates in Luxembourg DTAs commonly reduce royalties to 0-5% (e.g., France 0%, Germany 5%) and interest to 0-10% (e.g., Germany 0% if not defaulted). For SCSp, payments are treated as made by the partners proportionately; each partner may be subject to source-country tax only if they have a Luxembourg PE.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Transfer Pricing Documentation (Master File and Local File) applies where the consolidated group turnover equals or exceeds EUR 50 million and intercompany transactions exceed: EUR 1 million for services, EUR 2 million for financial transactions, EUR 5 million for purchases of goods (e.g., raw materials for dumplings), and EUR 250,000 for intangible property/royalties. In the absence of a local file, the Luxembourg tax authority may estimate taxable profit under Article 56 LIR.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no formal Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) similar to UAE, but the substance doctrine is embedded in the GAAR (Article 6 AEIL), the ‘abuse of law’ concept, and Article 9 BEPS hybrid rules. An SCSp operating an industrial frozen-dumpling factory must demonstrate real manufacturing presence in Luxembourg: qualified personnel, production facilities, warehouse and inventory at risk, board/manager decision-making, and proportionate working capital in the SCSp. A pure ‘letter-box’ SCSp distributing all profits to a zero-tax jurisdiction will be disregarded for treaty purposes and exposed to fiscal recharacterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate suppression or falsification of the frozen-dumpling factory's turnover, creation of fictitious invoices, or transfer of manufacturing profits to a non-resident low-tax entity without any commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment for 10 years, withdrawal of treaty benefits, default interest at 0.6%/month, fine up to EUR 250,000 (or 2x tax evaded), prosecution under the General Tax Law and Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and gérants are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax and penalties; Luxembourg courts may issue travel bans, freezing orders, and custodial sentences up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp lacks economic presence: no staff, no factory, no local management, profits passively channelled to a tax haven without operational purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority may disregard the SCSp and attribute the income directly to the ultimate controlling entity; recharacterization as an abusive arrangement; penalties of 20% to 40% of the tax underassessed; loss of treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Promoters and managers face personal liability for unpaid taxes under the fiscal unity doctrine, potential removal from commercial register, and professional disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp accepting unverified third-party funds or payments through Swift LC/TT without beneficial ownership disclosure; non-submission of AML/KYC statements; failure to appoint an authorized PFS or comply with FATF standards in the food-export trade.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to EUR 1 million and possible criminal imprisonment up to 5 years for deliberate laundering; confiscation of assets; administrative sanction of revocation of business license for the factory under article 115 of the amended law of 12 November 2004.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be criminally prosecuted as beneficial owners; travel bans and asset freezes are standard; civil liability towards the State for damage caused by laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp pays excessive management fees or discounts on dim-sum sales to a foreign affiliate, or uses a TNMM/CUP method without contemporaneous documentation, thereby eroding Luxembourg taxable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income to arm's length, late payment interest, 10% penalty for failure to file TP documentation, and potential criminal penalty if documents are falsified.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the additional tax if they signed intercompany contracts that were artificial and they failed to obtain independent valuation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File Annual Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission of Form 1001/SCSp annex by 30 June with no request for extension; automatic ex-officio assessment based on industry benchmarks without deduction of actual factory costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Ex-officio assessment, 10% increase on the assessed tax, fixed fine of up to EUR 7,500, monthly interest 0.6%, and administrative injunction imposing closure of the commercial kitchen.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant is personally liable for the fine and for any tax shortfall if the default is willful; habitual default may trigger director disqualification under the Commercial Code.
